correctness.rationale: For every existing nontrivial symmetric \(2\)-\((v,k,\lambda)\) design with \(2\le\lambda\le k-2\), the exact incidence identity \(MM^{\mathsf T}=(k-\lambda)I+\lambda J\) reduces the graph dipole equation to a scalar inverse on the zero-sum subspace. The explicit point and block voltages solve the complete Laplacian equation. Seven incidence edge classes exhaust all \(vk\) edges, with multiplicities fixed by pair-replication and constant block intersections; their currents have the asserted strict signs. Summing positive and negative currents proves the cut norm. The diagonal \(Q_{ee}\) is the effective resistance and belongs to \((0,1)\), so complementary column sums equal cut column sums plus \(1-2Q_{ee}\). Both operators are real symmetric, giving matching endpoint norms, and the comparison formula is strictly positive for \(k\ge4\). Four independently constructed incidence graphs have had all \(346\) grounded-inverse projection columns recomputed exactly and matched; these tests supplement, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The exact design-parameter-only column sums for canonical cut and cycle projections were compared by implication with source claims on Hamming/discrete-torus projection norms, symmetric-design incidence spectra, metric dimension, general electrical flow bounds and nearest graph-incidence cases. None of the inspected primary mathematical statements entails these absolute-current equalities. Relevant historical claim exclusions do not rest on title matching: projective-plane incidence requires lambda=1, crown graphs have lambda=k-1, general 3-design results need a triple-incidence axiom that fails for the (11,5,2) biplane. The existence of alternative formulations in less-indexed resistance literature remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: Symmetric \(2\)-design incidence graphs are natural bipartite distance-regular objects including biplanes and projective point-hyperplane designs. The two exact endpoint norms measure cut/cycle electrical-current amplification and are not fixed by diagonal effective resistance alone. The theorem establishes a parameter-only law across every existing nontrivial realization without needing flag transitivity and proves strict ordering of the complementary projections. It also gives a reproducible collection of concrete exact cases while leaving the design-existence question separate. This is a motivated natural complete classification, not a relabeling, arbitrary finite slice, or bare numerical experiment.
